content.title: The Winner of The Voice Season 29 Is Officially Revealed
content.text: From the outset, the competition was always going to be fierce, pitting the best of the best against one another in a friendly but serious contest. And that's just the Coaches. The Voice: Battle of Champions Coaches Adam Levine, Kelly Clarkson, and John Legend began Season 29 as amicable rivals, eager to show that they had the know-how to recruit and guide the best Artists.How to WatchOver the course of the competition, however, it got personal, as they became deeply invested in the potential careers of the Artists on their teams. By the time they reached The Voice Season 29 Finale, they each truly wanted the best for their representatives in the Top 4.Legend saw himself in piano player Lucas West, Clarkson was constantly in awe of teens Liv Ciara and Mikenley Brown, and Levine was beside himself with praise every time Alexia Jayy opened her mouth. "Listening to you sing, it's a privilege," Levine gushed during rehearsals on Finale night. RELATED: Stream New Episodes of The Voice: Battle of Champions the Next Day on PeacockAll four of the Finalists deserved their spots on that stage, and any one of them could easily have gone home with the trophy. But at the end of the night, only one did. Here's who won The Voice: Battle of Champions... Team Adam's Alexia Jayy won The Voice: Battle of ChampionsCovering "Lady Marmalade" by Patti LaBelle and "One and Only" by Adele, Jayy proved beyond a doubt why Levine kept insisting that she had one of the best voices he'd ever heard. "Alexia is one of the best vocalists I've had on my team. Every time she performs, she just nails it," Levine said in rehearsals before the results were revealed. "She's always game-ready. Alexia should be a household name." Jayy also opened up about her own passion for music and how her Coach had helped her gain the confidence necessary to deliver such bold performances."Music is like my other baby and presenting it to the world is scary, but being with Adam, I went from complete nervous[ness] to sitting in a room with one of my favorite artists singing all of these legendary songs — and I'm having fun! This gave me a new love for music," Jayy revealed about her time on the show. And that was before she won The Voice.RELATED: The Voice Season 29: The Ultimate Episode-by-Episode Guide for Super FansThe Alabama native and mother of two has been a frontrunner from the start, when she earned the first Triple Chair Turn of the season during her Blind Audition, and with her family at home supporting her, she managed to hit all the right notes in every round after. "I'd say I can't believe it, but I can. There's no one more deserving of this honor," Levine said after the voting results were revealed. "This was Alexia's night and I'm really proud of her," Clarkson said as she began to tear up. "She's so gifted, and honestly to see this woman who’s 31 years old and like, 'Where have you been?'""She was just consistently stunning and beautiful, magical. Truly happy she won the show," Legend added. The Voice: Battle of Champions full voting resultsThe in-studio audience declared Alexia Jayy as the winner of The Voice: Battle of Champions, and here's how the rest of the votes shook out: Winner! Alexia JayySecond place: Liv CiaraThird place: Lucas WestFourth place: Mikenley Brown After the full results were announced and Jayy was showered with confetti on stage, she called the biggest fan in her life — her mother. "Mama, I won! I won, I won, I won!" Jayy said through tears on FaceTime with her mom, who proudly said, "You did it!""I cannot believe I won The Voice!" Jayy later told cameras backstage. "I get to take this back home to my babies! Oh my God!"
